concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor supplied no new admissible evidence of actual current-release disclosure text or an approved release artifact containing the limitation; this concern was only reframed.
The Actor expressly conceded there is no reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or risk-acceptance record in evidence; the policy predicate remains unsatisfied.
The Actor narrowed the role of monitoring but did not provide a reviewed monitoring plan or approval artifact; the evidence still shows only an informal comment.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed and reframed the same record. That reframing is partly correct: prior approval is only contextual, aggregate readiness is relevant to launch readiness, and informal monitoring is not a substitute for current-release compliance predicates. But the core audit issue remains unresolved. Policy requires the current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material weaknesses for named launch use cases to be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance before certification. The admissible evidence still shows a current municipal permitting assistant regression, a policy disclosure requirement, and only an informal monitoring comment with no attached reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language. That is enough to preserve suspicion about present certification supportability on the existing record. This is not a clean caveated-compliance case, because caveats alone do not satisfy a missing documentation or approval predicate when the record does not show the required disclosure has actually been made.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation actually discloses the municipal permitting assistant regression as a material limitation for the named launch use case.
No admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering the current subgroup regression before launch.

The monitoring rationale remains unsupported as a certification predicate because the record contains only an informal monitoring comment with no reviewed attachment, owner acceptance, or governance approval.
